PAPERS.title: Associations of individual exposure to particulate matter with next-day physical activity and sedentary behaviour in older adults: a micro-longitudinal study
PAPERS.pm: Personal air-quality monitors (waking hours, 5 days) vs area-level PM2.5/PM10
PAPERS.n: Micro-longitudinal preprint: 67 UK adults aged 50-85 wore personal air-quality monitors (waking hours) and 24-h accelerometers for five days (304 person-days). Within-person mixed models: a higher-than-usual day (+1 IQR, i.e. +2.6 ug/m3 PM2.5 above the person's mean) was followed by 8 min less light activity (95% CI -14 to -2) and 483 fewer steps (-855 to -82); for PM10 (+2.8 ug/m3), 8 min less LPA (-13 to -3), 8 min more sedentary time (0 to 15) and 412 fewer steps. No MVPA association, and none with area-level PM. Not peer reviewed; the monitor model and any calibration are not stated; a 2.6 ug/m3 contrast is within typical optical-sensor error, so residual weather or illness confounding of day-to-day behaviour is the main threat. Relevance: high - the association exists only in personal-sensor exposure, not area estimates.

PAPERS.title: Spatiotemporal variability, trends, and health risk assessment of ambient PM2.5 and PM10 in Bangladesh during 2018-2025.
PAPERS.pm: 16 DoE continuous monitoring stations, PM2.5 and PM10, 2018-2025
PAPERS.n: Analysis of 2018-2025 PM2.5 and PM10 from the 16 Department of Environment continuous stations in Bangladesh, with seasonal Mann-Kendall trends and ELCR/HQ risk indices. Every station exceeded national standards and WHO guidelines every year. Network annual mean PM2.5 fell from 91.54 to 77.64 ug/m3 (-15.2%) and PM10 from 155.7 to 132.3 (-15.0%), non-monotonically, rebounding after the 2020 minimum; winter/monsoon ratios were ~4.2 (PM2.5) and 3.0 (PM10). Most seasonal trends were not significant. The authors note kriging performed poorly and was used only for display - 16 stations cannot map a country of 170 million. ELCR applied to PM2.5 mass is a screening construct, not an epidemiological risk. Relevance: the station-data quality control is undescribed, and this network is exactly what low-cost sensor densification in Bangladesh would calibrate against.

PAPERS.title: Environmental exposures and mental health: longitudinal results from the German National Cohort (NAKO)
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only - environmental exposures and mental health in NAKO (by title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata-only record: Elsevier deposited title, authors and DOI on 27 Sep with no abstract; Crossref, Europe PMC and the publisher landing page returned nothing. The title indicates longitudinal analyses of environmental exposures and mental health in the German National Cohort; which exposures (air pollution, noise, greenness, heat) are included cannot be stated. NAKO's size (~200,000) makes it a priority retry. Nothing about exposure metric, sample size or estimates can be stated from the deposit, and this watch does not infer a method from a title.

PAPERS.title: Spatiotemporal Contamination Characteristics, Bacterial Community Structure, and Airflow-Mediated Transport of Bacterial Aerosols in a Pediatric Emergency Consulting Room.
PAPERS.design: Repeated field measurement with CFD simulation
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved culturable bacterial aerosol (Andersen-type stages), CFD deposition
PAPERS.n: One paediatric emergency consulting room: culturable airborne and surface bacteria, high-throughput sequencing and CFD of aerosol transport and deposition. Airborne culturable counts differed little between locations (well-mixed small room), surface deposition was heterogeneous, and 73.47% of bacterial aerosol was below 3.3 um; Staphylococcus was the core genus. CFD placed the consultation desk and floor at 79.71% of deposited particles, with high-risk zones around occupants. One room, culturable fraction only (typically <1% of total bacteria), and sampling duration and counts are not in the abstract. Relevance: marginal; bioaerosol is invisible to optical PM sensors, so ventilation decisions here need culture or fluorescence methods.
